rule: Capture the essence rather than exhaustive realism; know what to leave suggested.
Light should strike the subject at an angle rather than straight on, to bring out sculptural modelling and surface relief.
The standard shading convention assumes light coming over the viewer's left shoulder at about 45 degrees; shade the sides turned away from it and draw the cast shadows.
Foreground objects get the thickest lines, darkest shadows and brightest colors; distant ones get faint lines, soft shadows and subdued color.
Darker shade and stronger shadows belong in the foreground, becoming progressively lighter into the distance, reinforcing perspective.
Do not render the whole sheet at the same intensity; leave large areas lightly treated so the detailed areas gain tension and focus.
Distant repeated detail can be reduced to a single line or a hint; full detail belongs only in the foreground.
Balance a dominant direction in a composition with counter-lines in the other direction.
